edges.description: Transformed HRS cells recruit and shape a supportive inflammatory niche.
Like the HRS cell, the LP cell actively manipulates and depends on its supportive lymphocyte- and histiocyte-rich microenvironment.
JAK/STAT signaling supports inflammatory niche formation.
NF-kappaB signaling sustains the inflammatory tumor niche.
Constitutive NF-kappaB signaling cooperates with checkpoint-ligand upregulation to promote immune escape.
EBV-driven NF-kappaB activation reinforces the inflammatory tumor niche.

edges.description: The inflammatory niche is coupled to ineffective anti-tumor immunity.
The tumor-supported inflammatory niche contributes to nodal enlargement.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to B symptoms including fever.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to B symptoms including night sweats.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to systemic B symptoms including weight loss.
Loss of surface class I removes the CD8 cytotoxic recognition arm, so the residual anti-tumour response that the checkpoint axis acts on is the MHC-class-II-dependent one.

evidence.snippet: However, several variants were consistently detected in genes related to relevant signaling pathways, such as GM-CSF/IL-3, CBP/EP300, JAK/STAT, NF-kappaB, and numerous variants of genes affecting the B-cell receptor (BCR) pathway, such as BTK, CARD11, BCL10, among others.

nodes.description: One of two genetically separate antigen-presentation arms in classic Hodgkin lymphoma, kept apart from its class II sibling because the two reach immune escape by different immunological routes. Recurrent somatic B2M lesions disrupt beta-2-microglobulin, the invariant light chain every class I molecule needs to reach the cell surface, so HRS cells show deficient surface MHC class I and with it reduced CD8 cytotoxic T-cell recognition. This is a different mechanism from checkpoint-ligand-mediated inhibition of the T cells that do still recognise the tumour.

nodes.description: The class II counterpart. CIITA, the MHC class II transactivator, is recurrently broken or fused in a subset of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, so class II expression is lost and with it CD4 T-cell recognition. This arm is the one that bears on treatment: HRS-cell MHC class II expression, not class I, predicts complete remission on PD-1 blockade, which is why the two arms are curated as separate nodes rather than as one antigen-presentation node.
